General Workflow: Step-by-Step Scripting Guide

Workflow.Rmd

Introduction

This guide walks you through building and executing a complete livestock environmental and nutritional assessment in R from scratch using herdr.

Whether you are modeling a single dairy farm, an intensive swine or poultry operation, or a national inventory across regions, following this structured workflow ensures full consistency across IPCC Tier 2 greenhouse gases, upstream feed LCA & water deprivation (EF 3.1 / AWARE), agroecological land competition, and edible protein outputs.

1. Installation & Environment Setup

Step 1: Install and Load herdr

Install the package directly from GitHub:

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}

remotes::install_github("JuanCBM99/herdr")
library(herdr)

Step 2: Initialize Your Working Directory

Run herdr_init() in your R console or project root:

herdr_init()

This generates three standard folders:

  • user_data/: The active working directory containing editable CSV scenario templates and reference libraries (ipcc_coefficients.csv, ipcc_mm.csv, feed_characteristics.csv, mapping.csv). Background databases (forages.parquet, fao_crops.parquet, fao_trade_matrix.parquet, ecoalim.parquet) are resolved automatically via bundled assets and central cache.
  • Examples/: Pre-configured baseline datasets (Blank_IPCC_2019, Level1_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015, Level2_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015, Monogastric_Example, Video_Example) ready to use as templates.
  • output/: Destination directory where results (total_emissions_and_land_use.csv and product_intensities.csv) are automatically saved.

2. Project Architecture, Demographic Keys & Strict Taxonomy

All data tables in herdr are linked using four primary demographic cohort keys:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          PRIMARY DEMOGRAPHIC COHORT KEYS                               │
├─────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────────────────┤
│  farm_id        │  animal_tag             │  region      │  subregion                  │
│  (Mandatory)    │  (Mandatory)            │  (Optional)  │  (Optional)                 │
│  e.g., "farm_1" │  e.g., "dairy_cows"     │  e.g., spain │  e.g., "north"              │
└─────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

⚠️ Critical Join & Ordering Rules: 1. Exact Key Matching: Every unique combination of farm_id, animal_tag, region, and subregion declared in livestock_census.csv must match the definition, weight, and manure tables exactly. Identifiers are strictly lowercase with underscores (no spaces or uppercase letters). 2. Spatial vs. Management Grouping: Together, (farm_id, region, subregion) define a physical farm/location. Different management phases or housing variants within the same farm (e.g., lactating vs. dry cows, or caged vs. free-range hens) should share the same (farm_id, region, subregion) and be distinguished via animal_tag so their enterprise intensities integrate properly in output tables. 3. Preserved Row Order: The top-to-bottom row order in livestock_census.csv is preserved in all output tables (results$totals, results$intensities) and bar charts (plot_herdr_results()).

Strict Taxonomy (animal_type, animal_subtype, production_role)

To guarantee unambiguous biophysical allocation and manure factor lookups, herdr enforces strict values in ruminant_definitions.csv and monogastric_definitions.csv (no legacy aliases or empty strings allowed):

Table animal_type (Strict) animal_subtype (Strict) production_role (Strict)
ruminant_definitions.csv cattle, sheep, goat dairy or meat mature, replacement, or slaughter
monogastric_definitions.csv swine meat mature, replacement, or slaughter
monogastric_definitions.csv poultry meat or layer mature, replacement, or slaughter

3. Preparing Input Tables (user_data/)

You can edit the CSV templates located in user_data/ using any spreadsheet editor, the interactive Shiny App (run_herdr_app()), or programmatically in R. For the full column-by-column schema, see the Technical Data Dictionary.

Summary of Required Input Tables:

Domain File Primary Purpose Key Columns
1. Population livestock_census.csv Animal head counts (AAP) & display order farm_id, animal_tag, region, subregion, population
2. Body Weights livestock_weights.csv Weight boundaries & cycle lengths adult_weight_kg, productive_period_days, initial_weight_kg, final_weight_kg
3. Definitions ruminant_definitions.csv
monogastric_definitions.csv 		Species taxonomy, IPCC/FEDNA traits & yields animal_type, animal_subtype, production_role, diet_tag, replacement_rate
4. Feeding Rations diet_profiles.csv
diet_ingredients.csv 		Macro shares & micro feedstuffs forage_share, concentrate_share, ingredient, ingredient_share
5. Manure Systems manure_management.csv Housing, storage & pasture shares system_base, system_variant, system_climate, b_0, allocation

Two Golden Rules for Diets & Manure:

  1. Diet Proportions: In diet_profiles.csv, forage_share + concentrate_share + milk_share + milk_replacer_share must sum to 100%. In diet_ingredients.csv, ingredient_share values must sum to 100% within each active category.
  2. Manure Allocations: In manure_management.csv, the sum of allocation for each unique cohort must equal exactly 1.0 (100%).

4. Executing the Environmental Assessment

4.1. Consolidated Pipeline (generate_impact_assessment)

The fastest and most complete way to run the model is generate_impact_assessment(). It executes the entire upstream chain (energy balance, DMI, enteric fermentation, manure management, upstream feed LCA & water deprivation, agroecological land use, and GLEAM production) and returns a named list with two dataframes:

  • results$totals (saved to output/total_emissions_and_land_use.csv): Table 1 — Absolute Bio-Environmental Inventory & Per-Head Metrics for every cohort.
  • results$intensities (saved to output/product_intensities.csv): Table 2 — Enterprise-Integrated Commercial & Nutritional Intensities across milk, meat, eggs, wool, edible protein, and Mottet (2017) Protein FCRs.
library(herdr)

# Run full assessment for reference year 2024
results <- generate_impact_assessment(
  farm_country    = "Spain",
  year            = 2024,
  automatic_cycle = FALSE,
  gwp_report      = "AR5",
  saveoutput      = TRUE
)

# Inspect Table 1: Absolute cohort inventory & per-head footprints
head(results$totals)

# Inspect Table 2: Enterprise-integrated product & protein intensities
head(results$intensities)

How Table 1 (totals) and Table 2 (intensities) Work Together:

Output Table Scope & Purpose Key Columns
Table 1 (results$totals) Direct Cohort Inventory: Reports the exact direct emissions, feed intake, land use, water deprivation, and per-head footprint of each individual cohort (mature, replacement, slaughter). CO2eq_enteric, CO2eq_manure, CO2eq_N2O_direct, CO2eq_N2O_indirect, CO2eq_feed_fossil_Gg, CO2eq_feed_luc_Gg, CO2eq_Total_Gg, CO2eq_cradle_to_farm_Gg, Land_cropland_m2, Land_grassland_convertible_m2, Land_grassland_unconvertible_m2, Land_m2, Water_feed_m3, CO2eq_Total_head, CO2eq_cradle_to_farm_head, Land_head, Water_head
Table 2 (results$intensities) Enterprise-Integrated Intensities: Groups cohorts by enterprise (farm_id, region, subregion, animal_type, animal_subtype) and attributes non-commercial rearing/breeding overhead (replacement and mature breeders) to commercial outputs (milk, meat, egg, wool, protein). milk_FPCM_kg, meat_carcass_weight_kg, egg_fresh_kg, wool_kg, total_protein_kg, GHG_intensity_*, GHG_cradle_to_farm_*, Land_intensity_*, Water_intensity_*, Protein_FCR_total, Protein_FCR_cropland

4.2. Modular Step-by-Step Execution

Researchers seeking intermediate physiological outputs can run individual modules sequentially:

# 1. Animal Demography & Population Balance
pop_data <- calculate_population(automatic_cycle = FALSE)

# 2. Weighted Nutritional Diet Characteristics
feed_vars <- calculate_weighted_variable()

# 3. Gross Energy Intake (GE) & Monogastric Metabolizable Energy (ME)
ge_data <- calculate_ge()
mono_me <- calculate_monogastric_energy()

# 4. Dry Matter Intake (DMI) & Volatile Solids (VS)
dmi_data <- calculate_DMI()
vs_data  <- calculate_vs()

# 5. Enteric Methane Emissions (CH4)
enteric_emiss <- calculate_emissions_enteric()

# 6. Manure Methane & Nitrous Oxide (CH4, Direct & Indirect N2O)
manure_ch4     <- calculate_CH4_manure()
manure_n2o_dir <- calculate_N2O_direct_manure()
manure_n2o_vol <- calculate_N2O_indirect_volatilization()
manure_n2o_lea <- calculate_N2O_indirect_leaching()

# 7. Upstream Feed LCA (Fossil vs LUC CO2e) & AWARE Water Deprivation
feed_lca <- calculate_feed_emissions()

# 8. Feed Land Use Footprint & FAO Trade Origin
land_data <- calculate_land_use(farm_country = "Spain", year = 2024)

# 9. Animal Productivity & Edible Human Protein (GLEAM)
prod_data <- calculate_production()

5. Visualizing & Benchmarking Results

Pass results directly to plot_herdr_results() to generate publication-ready stacked ggplot2 charts. You can combine any impact_category ("ghg", "land", "water", "overview", "fcr") with any functional_unit ("total", "product", "milk", "meat", "egg", "wool", "protein", "head", "fcr"):

# 1. Multi-Impact Overview (Carbon, Land, and Water panels side by side)
p_overview <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_type", "region"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "overview",
  functional_unit = "total"
)

# 2. Carbon Footprint per kg Commercial Product (Scope 1 + Feed Fossil + Feed LUC)
p_product_ghg <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_type", "animal_subtype"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "ghg",
  functional_unit = "product"
)

# 3. Agroecological Land Footprint per kg Edible Protein (m2 / kg human protein)
p_protein_land <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_tag"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "land",
  functional_unit = "protein"
)

# 4. AWARE Water Deprivation per Animal Head (m3 depriv. / head / year)
p_head_water <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_type"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "water",
  functional_unit = "head"
)

# 5. Protein Feed Conversion & Human Food Competition (Mottet et al. 2017)
p_fcr <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_type", "animal_subtype"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "fcr",
  functional_unit = "fcr"
)

# Display chart
print(p_product_ghg)

# Export chart to disk
ggplot2::ggsave("output/product_intensity_chart.png", plot = p_product_ghg, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

6. Common Issues & Troubleshooting

Issue / Alert Cause Solution
Missing Cohorts Error An animal_tag in Census is missing in definitions, weights, or manure tables. Ensure all 4 keys (farm_id, animal_tag, region, subregion) match across all input tables.
Invalid animal_subtype or production_role A non-standard value (e.g. beef, other, or blank) was entered in definitions. Use strictly dairy or meat for ruminants, meat for swine, meat or layer for poultry, and mature, replacement, or slaughter for production_role.
Shares do not sum to 100% Diet category or ingredient proportions do not sum to 100. Adjust forage_share, concentrate_share, etc. in diet_profiles.csv, or ingredient_share in diet_ingredients.csv.
Manure allocation != 1.0 Allocations for a cohort do not sum to 1.0. Adjust allocation values in manure_management.csv so their sum equals exactly 1.0 per cohort.
Unknown Ingredient An ingredient in diets is missing in reference libraries. Add the ingredient to feed_characteristics.csv and mapping.csv (see Adding a New Ingredient).
